headline: High-risk data leakage and cascading-error paths exist because Replit Agent can read/write broad workspace data while LightZero is a non-runnable game-playing component with no isolation or verification boundary.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A direct prompt-injection bridge is not documented: LightZero has no filesystem, network, or MCP surfaces, while Replit Agent operates in a Repl workspace with files and shell. The only plausible pathway is unusual manual copy/paste or file handoff into Replit, so the blast radius is limited and not default.
conditions: IF LightZero outputs are manually pasted into Replit Agent prompts or files
IF Replit Agent is instructed to treat imported text as authoritative instructions
mitigations: Keep LightZero outputs out of Replit prompts unless sanitized
Use a fixed delimiter and instruction prefix for pasted content
Review any imported text before execution
Disable copy/paste handoff for untrusted content
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Replit Agent can read and write Repl workspace files and handles secrets and deployment configuration, while LightZero itself has no data surfaces. If LightZero artifacts are placed into the shared Repl workspace, Replit Agent can ingest them and potentially expose secrets or source code in its outputs; this is a default workspace-risk pathway, not a provable block.
conditions: IF LightZero artifacts are stored in the same Repl workspace as Replit Agent
IF the workspace contains secrets or deployment configuration
mitigations: Move sensitive files out of the shared Repl workspace
Rotate any secrets present in the workspace
Restrict Replit Agent to a minimal subdirectory
Audit generated outputs for secret echoes
requires-engineering: separate sensitive and non-sensitive workspaces

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LightZero cannot write files, modify git, or use network, so it cannot contend for mutable resources with Replit Agent. Replit Agent does have broad write and git capabilities, but without overlapping write authority from LightZero there is no meaningful conflict beyond manual orchestration mistakes.
conditions: IF LightZero is wrapped by an external orchestrator that gives it write access not shown in the profile
mitigations: Keep LightZero read-only in the pair
Avoid concurrent edits to the same Repl files
Use git branches for Replit Agent changes
Lock the workspace during Replit Agent writes
requires-engineering: add file-locking in the orchestrator

D_cascading_error.rationale: LightZero is a game-playing system and Replit Agent is a coding agent that can act on workspace files and deployments. If LightZero-generated outputs are fed into Replit Agent as facts or plans, Replit Agent may act on them without verification, creating a default cascading-error path even though LightZero is not a general-purpose factual source.
conditions: IF LightZero outputs are used as inputs to Replit Agent tasks
IF Replit Agent is allowed to modify files or deployments based on those outputs without review
mitigations: Require human review before Replit Agent acts on LightZero output
Mark LightZero output as untrusted data
Add a verification checklist for any downstream action
Limit Replit Agent to draft-only mode for imported content
requires-engineering: implement output provenance checks

E_compliance.rationale: Replit Agent explicitly touches secrets, source code, and deployment configuration in a cloud Repl, while LightZero is open-source and non-runnable. If regulated or sensitive data is placed into the Repl, Replit Agent's cloud handling can create residency or retention concerns; LightZero is not the compliance driver, so only Replit is cited.
conditions: IF regulated data or secrets are stored in the Repl workspace
IF the deployment or secret-handling policy differs from the data's required residency or retention
mitigations: Do not place regulated data in the Repl
Remove unused secrets from the workspace
Review Replit retention and export settings
Use synthetic data for development
requires-engineering: segregate regulated workloads
